title: Coffee Shop SEO and AEO: Lessons From Andytown, Double Black, Delah and Philz
summary: Compare Andytown, Double Black, Delah and Philz for practical coffee shop SEO and AEO lessons on locations, hours, menus, and accurate answers.
body_markdown:
Could a customer tell whether your coffee shop is open at 10:30 on a Sunday night? What if two pages on your own website gave different answers?


That question is a useful starting point for coffee shop SEO and answer engine optimization, or AEO: helping people find useful, accurate information through search and AI answers. Before trying to win a recommendation, make the basic facts easy to find and trust.


We compared the public websites for four San Francisco locations: Andytown on Lawton Street, Double Black on Cole Street, Delah Coffee on Fourth Street, and Philz in the Castro. Each illustrates a different part of the job, from identifying the right branch to explaining a menu in readable text.


**This is a dated website comparison, not a ranking contest.** We reviewed the pages on October 20, 2026. We did not measure Google Maps positions or test recommendations from ChatGPT or other assistants. Published details can change, and a website discrepancy does not tell us which hours the shop actually keeps.


## What SEO and AEO mean for a coffee shop


Local search engine optimization helps a business become discoverable in relevant nearby searches. Google says its local results depend mainly on relevance, distance, and prominence: how well the business matches the search, how close it is, and how well known it is. Its[local ranking guidance](https://support.google.com/business/answer/7091?hl=en) recommends complete, accurate business information.


AEO describes the work of making information useful to systems that answer questions. A diner might ask an assistant about closing time, oat milk, a particular drink, or pickup ordering. Accurate source material gives those questions a clearer basis for an answer; it does not guarantee that an assistant will use it.


For Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode,[Google says established SEO practices still apply](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) . There is no extra AI-specific optimization requirement or special structured data needed. Structured data is machine-readable information about a page; adding it cannot resolve contradictory facts on that page.


## The four-shop comparison


Public website observations, October 20, 2026 Coffee shop and location What the website shows What owners can learn


Andytown
3655 Lawton Street A branch entry with address, hours, directions, and an order-ahead link. Keep the exact location clear when one brand has several cafés.


Double Black
925 Cole Street Text FAQs explain the café and answer practical questions; menus are presented as images. Keep useful answers in text, including menu details.


Delah Coffee
370 Fourth Street Two official pages disagree about closing times. Resolve inconsistent information before adding more content.


Philz Coffee
549 Castro Street A dedicated branch page groups local details, hours, and customer links. Give each branch a useful destination, even within a larger chain.


## Andytown: make the right branch easy to identify


[Andytown's locations page](https://andytownsf.com/pages/locations) gives its Lawton Street café a separate entry with an Outer Sunset description, street address, daily schedule, directions, and order-ahead link. Other cafés have their own entries and schedules.


The lesson is branch identity. A customer asking when Andytown closes needs an answer for a specific café. For a business with multiple locations, repeating the brand name without the address or neighborhood leaves room for confusion.


**Apply this:** Give every location a clearly labeled section or page. Keep the street, neighborhood, phone number, and hours together. Then check that the corresponding Google Business Profile and ordering destination refer to that same location.


A dedicated URL can be useful when a café needs its own menu, accessibility details, or ordering instructions. This comparison does not establish that a separate page is necessary to rank.


## Double Black: answer the questions a new customer actually has


[Double Black's café page](https://yardsale.day/pages/double-black) explains its relationship to Yardsale, the retail store that houses it. Its text FAQs cover the address, hours, dietary choices, and alternative milks. That gives a visitor practical information without requiring them to infer it from photos.


The same page presents its menus as images. Those can be attractive, but adding readable menu text would let customers find specific drinks and prices without interpreting a picture. Image-based menus are not proof of a search penalty; text is simply a more direct way to provide the information.


**Apply this:** Put the café's name and location in a clear introduction, especially if it sits inside another business. Add short, factual answers to real customer questions and keep menu text current alongside any designed menu images.


A question-and-answer layout can help readers. It is not a promise that an AI assistant will cite the page.


## Delah Coffee: fix conflicting facts before chasing visibility


For the Fourth Street location,[Delah's locations page](https://delahcoffee.com/locations/) published an 11pm closing time every day. Its[contact page](https://delahcoffee.com/contact/) showed 10pm closing Monday through Thursday and Sunday, with 11pm on Friday and Saturday.


That creates a concrete problem for someone checking whether they can visit at 10:30pm on Sunday. Both answers come from the business's own website. We have not confirmed the correct schedule with the operator.


**Apply this:** Confirm the real hours first, then reconcile the website, Google listing, and ordering schedule. Assign someone to update these surfaces whenever the schedule changes. The discrepancy demonstrates uncertainty, not evidence that the café lost rankings or sales.


## Philz: borrow a chain's approach to location pages


We used[Philz's Castro page](https://philzcoffee.com/locations/castro) as the chain comparison. It brings the address, phone number, day-by-day hours, neighborhood context, menu links, and a web-ordering link onto one branch page. App promotion is also present.


A small operator can use the same organization without copying the scale of a chain. A location page should help someone choose that café and take the next step, rather than only introducing the brand.


**Apply this:** Make directions, the menu, and available ordering options easy to reach. Check where every link goes. Customers should not have to discover that they selected the wrong branch after building an order.


The existence of a branch page does not prove that Philz performs better in local search or AI answers. We observed page organization, not an advantage in rankings.


## A coffee shop SEO checklist you can use today


### 1. Establish one verified set of business facts


Write down the exact name, address, phone number, regular hours, holiday exceptions, and customer-facing URLs for each location. Use operator-confirmed information as the reference. When public pages disagree, do not choose whichever answer appears most often.


### 2. Review your Google Business Profile


Check verification, the business category, location details, regular and special hours, photos, and the menu or ordering links available to your business. Ask for honest reviews and respond helpfully. Keep these tasks grounded in[Google's current guidance](https://support.google.com/business/answer/7091?hl=en) ; proximity remains part of local search, even with a complete profile.


### 3. Make the menu and practical answers readable


Publish important menu information as text, then supplement it with photography or a designed menu. Explain location-specific choices accurately: milk alternatives, food options, seating, and how pickup works. If an item rotates or sells out, say so instead of presenting availability as permanent.


### 4. Follow the customer path on a phone


Start with the listing link, open the website, find the menu, and follow the ordering path where one exists. Confirm the location before checkout. Record broken links, unexpected destinations, and unclear instructions separately. A café that does not offer online ordering does not have a broken ordering flow.


### 5. Measure actions that matter


Track website visits, direction requests, calls, and completed orders where the available tools support that measurement. Compare similar periods and note schedule or promotion changes. More impressions can be useful, but they are not the same as more café customers.


## How to test AI answers without inventing an AEO score


Start with factual questions, not a broad request for the best coffee in San Francisco. Use the exact café name and address so the test is about the right branch.


- What time does this location close on Sunday?
- Where is the café, and is it inside another business?
- Which milk alternatives does this location publish?
- What does its website say about vegan food?
- Does it provide a pickup-ordering link?


For each response, save the question, assistant and model, date, whether web search was enabled, the answer, and any cited sources. Classify the response as correct, incorrect, unanswered, or unverifiable against your verified business facts.


If you fix a source, repeat the same questions later and record what changes. One different answer does not prove that the edit caused the improvement. We did not run these assistant tests for the four shops in this article, so there is no measured AI-accuracy score here.


Broad recommendations need a different test. These shops occupy different neighborhoods, so searching “coffee near me” from one point cannot fairly rank their optimization work. Any visibility comparison needs a recorded search location, consistent queries, and repeated observations.


## What to fix first


Start with contradictions, then branch identity, then readable menus and usable links. Those changes help a customer make a decision even if an algorithm never rewards the work.


Use Andytown to think about distinguishing branches, Double Black to think about useful factual answers, Delah to think about source consistency, and Philz to think about organizing a location page. The goal is a customer who can confidently decide where to go and what to order.


If your listing sends people to a website that makes those steps difficult, review the whole journey. Avocado builds[restaurant and café websites with online ordering](https://avocadopos.com/websites) ; our[café and quick-service POS](https://avocadopos.com/quick-service) connects the order to operations. A useful website should earn its place by helping guests complete a task.


## Sources and scope


This comparison uses the official pages linked above, reviewed October 20, 2026. It covers four deliberately selected San Francisco locations, including a chain location; it is not a representative survey or a review of food, service, ownership practices, or business performance. We did not access private analytics, inspect live Google profiles, validate structured data, complete orders, or collect assistant answers.


Observed website details and our suggested improvements are different kinds of evidence. We link the pages for the observations and label the actions as recommendations. Recheck time-sensitive information before planning a visit.
